scenarios.title: Read+Update discovery carries operations and no Transactional member

requirements.selectedText: `operations` is required in Read+Update and Transactional and prohibited in Read. The history, receipt, snapshot, changefeed, and Event members are required only in Transactional and prohibited in both lower profiles.

scenarios.title: The Operation Directory lists exactly the six singleton targets plus sequence

requirements.selectedText: A Read+Update Scope's directory contains exactly the six singleton targets plus `sequence`:

scenarios.title: create-bead returns the created postimage with an allocated or honored id

requirements.selectedText: If `id` is omitted, the authority allocates one.
`created` and `updated` carry `resource`, the complete Resource record as a `GET` of its URL would now return it

scenarios.title: update-bead-properties applies the patch and retains the revision on a semantic no-op

requirements.selectedText: Applying the patch must yield a JSON object satisfying every effective Type schema.
A semantic no-op update, defined under [Revisions](#revisions), succeeds with outcome `updated` and the retained revision.

scenarios.title: delete-bead returns the deleted identity and refuses a Bead with live incident Links

requirements.selectedText: `deleted` carries `deleted`, the absolute canonical URL of the removed Resource, and no record: deletion mints no version.
After a Bead or Link is deleted, ordinary `GET`, `view=properties`, and, for a Bead, `view=links` return the same `404` `resource-not-found` problem used for an unknown or non-visible identity.
`incident-links-exist`: a Bead deletion reached while a live Link is incident upon the Bead.

scenarios.title: create-link canonicalizes endpoint spellings and echoes a pin byte-identically

requirements.selectedText: A durable relative endpoint reference resolves against the canonical Scope URL, not against the request URL or the containing Link URL, and must name a live Bead.
The pin is provenance, not a constraint: an authority stores and echoes it byte-identically, compares it only for equality, and performs no semantic validation, dereferencing, or interpretation

scenarios.title: update-link-properties returns the Link postimage and moves only the Link's own revision

requirements.selectedText: `created` and `updated` carry `resource`, the complete Resource record as a `GET` of its URL would now return it
An owned Link remains a first-class Link with its own URL and its own revision: a caller addresses, reads, and updates it there like any other Link.

scenarios.title: delete-link returns the deleted identity and the Link then reads as 404

requirements.selectedText: `deleted` carries `deleted`, the absolute canonical URL of the removed Resource, and no record: deletion mints no version.
After a Bead or Link is deleted, ordinary `GET`, `view=properties`, and, for a Bead, `view=links` return the same `404` `resource-not-found` problem used for an unknown or non-visible identity.

scenarios.title: Owned-Link mutations carry sourceRevision and version the source; unowned ones do neither

requirements.selectedText: Every mutation of an owned Link versions the source Bead.

When the mutated Link's type is owned by its source Bead's declared Type, the result additionally carries `sourceRevision`, the source Bead's resulting revision, on creation, update, and deletion alike
`sourceRevision` is absent from every other result.
Creating or deleting a Link does not mutate an in-Scope endpoint Bead or change that Bead's Resource revision

scenarios.title: The attribution input is recorded on every minted version and absent from a no-op

requirements.selectedText: An operation that mints more than one version records its one attribution on every version it mints
a write whose `properties` are a no-op mints no revision and records no attribution.

scenarios.title: A matching expectedRevision applies and a stale one fails with revision-mismatch

requirements.selectedText: `expectedRevision` remains optional for updates and deletes, and it produces a conflict on mismatch.
`revision-mismatch`: the member's `expectedRevision` is not the Resource's current revision.

scenarios.title: A missing or malformed Idempotency-Key is rejected before execution

requirements.selectedText: A key outside the profile is rejected before execution with `malformed-request`, as is a singleton request that omits the field.

scenarios.title: A singleton retry under the same key returns the retained disposition without re-execution

requirements.selectedText: the key is retained with the same semantic identity: the authority does not execute the member and returns the retained disposition
A retained `created` result therefore always carries the same authority-allocated identity
a singleton whose key is retained, in flight, conflicting, or expired answers exactly as the corresponding sequence member would, as a direct response.

scenarios.title: The same key with different semantics fails with idempotency-conflict

requirements.selectedText: the key is retained with a different semantic identity: the member fails with `idempotency-conflict`, nothing executes, and the retained disposition is unchanged;

scenarios.title: A non-JSON request body is rejected with unsupported-media-type

requirements.selectedText: `unsupported-media-type`: a mutation-target request whose body media type is not `application/json`; media-type parameters are ignored.

scenarios.title: Mutation targets answer other methods with a bodyless 405 and Allow: POST

requirements.selectedText: A mutation target responds `405 Method Not Allowed` with `Allow: POST` to every other method, and the Operation Directory responds `405` with `Allow: GET, HEAD` to every method but those two

scenarios.title: Members run strictly in order and a failure leaves earlier successes committed

requirements.selectedText: starts members strictly in declaration order and never runs them in parallel;
commits each successful member immediately and never rolls it back because a later member fails;
continues after a failed member so later independent work can run;

scenarios.title: A binding is usable after its creating member commits; unavailable bindings fail only their member

requirements.selectedText: The binding becomes available only after the create commits.
a reference to a forward, unknown, failed, or wrong-kind binding fails that member with `binding-unavailable` rather than rejecting the request.

scenarios.title: A member problem carries its would-be status, operationIndex, and operationName inside 200 OK

requirements.selectedText: Each failed member contains the same Problem Details shape with its would-be `status`, its zero-based `operationIndex`, and, when the member declared one, its `operationName`.
Every entry carries `operationIndex`, the member's zero-based position in the request's `operations` array, and carries `operationName` exactly when the member declared `name`.

scenarios.title: An oversized member count, repeated key, or stray Idempotency-Key field is rejected before execution

requirements.selectedText: `operations` is bounded by `sequence.operations` when that limit is advertised; a longer sequence is rejected before execution with `limit-exceeded`.
Two members of one sequence MUST NOT carry the same `idempotencyKey`; a sequence that repeats a key is rejected before execution with `malformed-request`
a sequence request that carries the field is rejected before execution with `malformed-request`.

scenarios.title: A retried sequence returns every retained disposition at the present member's position

requirements.selectedText: the key is retained with the same semantic identity: the authority does not execute the member and returns the retained disposition, positioned with the present member's `operationIndex` and `operationName`;
The authority runs the remaining members to their terminal dispositions and retains those dispositions under their keys, so a retry recovers a lost response member by member.

scenarios.title: An unrelated mutation committed between two members is observed by the later member

requirements.selectedText: permits unrelated requests to interleave between members, taking no sequence-wide transaction, reservation, or lock.
Because unrelated mutations may interleave, a bound Resource may change or be deleted before a later member uses it.

scenarios.title: A concurrent duplicate fails with idempotency-in-progress and a later retry receives the retained disposition

requirements.selectedText: the key is in flight — the member that first presented it has not reached a terminal outcome: the member fails with `idempotency-in-progress`, the authority executes nothing and retains nothing for the presenting member, and a retry after the delay receives the retained disposition;

scenarios.title: A key presented after retention fails with idempotency-expired and never re-executes

requirements.selectedText: Presenting an expired key with the same semantic identity fails with `idempotency-expired`; the authority never executes the member again and never reports the discarded outcome.
An authority retains each retained disposition for at least `retention.idempotency` after the member's terminal outcome when it advertises that limit

scenarios.title: Every Read+Update code serializes with its exact family, status, retry, media type, and cache policy

requirements.selectedText: The Read+Update profile inherits the complete Read table unchanged and adds the rows below.
Each code fixes its HTTP status and retry disposition.
Scope-bounded representations that depend on authorization use `Cache-Control: private, no-store`.

scenarios.title: An inadmissible result fails with validation-failed and an uninstalled Type with type-not-installed

requirements.selectedText: `validation-failed`: the mutation is well-formed but its result is not admissible
A mutation that names an unavailable Type fails as `type-not-installed`; the mutation does not initiate installation.

scenarios.title: A supplied id that was ever committed, including a deleted one, fails with identity-taken

requirements.selectedText: If `id` is supplied, its canonical Resource URL must never previously have been committed for any Resource in the logical Scope. Deletion does not make it available again.
`identity-taken`: a supplied `id` whose canonical Resource URL was ever committed in the logical Scope, including a deleted one.

scenarios.title: A mutation that would cross a maximum endpoint multiplicity fails with aggregate-constraint-violation

requirements.selectedText: Authorities MUST produce serializable outcomes when concurrent mutations could cross a maximum.
`aggregate-constraint-violation`: the mutation would violate a Scope aggregate policy — in BDP v0, a maximum endpoint multiplicity.

scenarios.title: Every mutation response carries Cache-Control: private, no-store

requirements.selectedText: Mutation responses carry `Cache-Control: private, no-store`.
